The parties have agreed that the title is not part of the document. But it should also be noted that the same type of document was, except for its title, admitted into evidence as Exhibit 111. And Exhibit 111 appears to be another excerpt from the same book also. I'm just telling you so that I orient you on these MFI documents. 131, this is an order issued by -- I don't know if I'm going to pronounce it correctly, Cedomir Bulat, which was tendered by the Prosecution. Now, Witness Maksic stated that this document was not familiar to him and pointed out that the document does not indicate to whom it is addressed, and based on those comments the Defence objected to its admission. Now, another order by Kemal Bulat was admitted into evidence through expert witness Theunens on the 26th of January, and this is Exhibit 51. And it is just noteworthy that MFI 131 carries the same signature which is similar to the signature on Exhibit 51. Okay? And I don't know whether the parties would like to have these two documents admitted into evidence at this stage. Let's start with you, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no problem with that. I think that -- I think that's fine to have both of them admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic? In that event, may Exhibit 112, which was an MFI, please be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 112, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we do the same with Exhibit MFI 131?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as relates Exhibit MFI 241, this was a bulletin issued by the Federal Secretariat of National Defence on 3rd of December 1991, and introduced by the Defence during the hearing of Milan Babic's evidence. The Chamber marked this for identification because it lacked an English translation. It is unclear the Defence actually intended to tender the document into evidence as it only asked for -- to have it displayed, and the lack of translation was pointed out by the Prosecution before the Defence took any action to tender it into evidence. I think that the Prosecution had undertaken to find a translation. I don't know how far you've gone on that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we looked and this document has not been translated by the Prosecution. There is no -- we're not aware of a translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So does this therefore mean that it cannot be admitted into evidence, because the Chamber will be at sea about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think with respect to this document what I would suggest is that we -- we endeavour to get a translation of the document. We can -- we can request one. I'll take that on. And then maybe we could defer this discussion until we have a translation and have an opportunity to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Prosecution is reminded the whole fact was defer the last time because the Prosecution was going to try and get it translated. If you could do that as soon as you possibly can Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, we will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The other MFIs that remain relate to Mr. Ban's testimony. Now -- I see you want to stand up, Mr. Milovancevic. Let me see if I can preempt you from standing. We are not talking here about whether to admit Mr. Babic's evidence in its entirety or not. That is still a different topic which we will talk about later. There are motions that are being prepared by the parties. We're talking here about just these exhibits. And if we say now that we admit these exhibits, obviously they will suffer the same fate as the fate that will be suffered by the entire evidence of Mr. Babic when that point is decided at that time. So we are not talking about Mr. Babic's entire evidence. What shall we do with these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In that event, then, I guess you also have no objection, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Then MFI Exhibits 200, 201, 202, 223, 225, 226, 227, 228, 231, and 233 are admitted into evidence, and may they be given, I believe, corresponding exhibits numbers, Mr. Court Officer.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They shall, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge Nosworthy was attracting myself to Exhibit 241, but I think we have dealt with that already. Okay. That brings us to the end of today's session. I'm sorry we took an extra 20 minutes, but at least this avoids us coming back in the afternoon. I hope everybody appreciates that. Thank you very much. Happy Easter weekend everybody. Let's come back fresh and ready to work on Tuesday. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of April, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
